body:
A full sweep of live Kalshi and Polymarket gold contracts turned up zero net-positive cross-platform opportunities today. That's a normal outcome — most scans find nothing, and it simply means the two platforms' order books are priced consistently with each other once fees and spreads are accounted for.

The two venues are structured very differently, which is worth understanding rather than treating as an inefficiency. Kalshi's contracts are single-point settlement bets — e.g., Gold above $4,330.99 on September 30, 2026 at 5:00 PM EDT (bid 0.55 / ask 0.65) or the year-end $4,300 or above contract (bid 0.70 / ask 0.72) — which pay out based on the spot price at one specific moment. Polymarket's contracts are mostly touch bets, like Will Gold hit (LOW) $4,300 in September (bid 0.64 / ask 0.70), which pay out if gold reaches that level at any point during the window, even briefly. A touch contract will almost always price higher than a settle contract at the same strike because there are many more paths to touching a level than to closing above it — that structural gap explains most of the apparent spread between similarly-priced contracts on the two sites, not a tradeable edge.

One spot worth noting for anyone scanning the book manually: Polymarket's Gold Up or Down on September 8 contract shows a wide 0.16 bid / 0.67 ask spread. That's a thin-book symptom rather than a signal — daily directional coin-flip markets tend to get little resting liquidity, so the quoted spread balloons even when nothing unusual is happening in the underlying. Overall, strike pricing across both platforms is internally consistent with gold trading somewhere in the low-$4,300s, and there's nothing in today's data that points to a mispricing worth flagging further.
headline: Gold markets scan finds no cross-platform arbitrage today
